senses.sense_definition: A highly toxic salt or chemical compound, such as sodium or potassium cyanide, notorious as a deadly poison and used in industrial processes.

examples.text: The detective immediately suspected foul play when tests revealed traces of <w>cyanide</w> in the victim's drink.
Workers at the gold mine were strictly trained in handling <w>cyanide</w> safely.

senses.sense_definition: Hydrogen cyanide in gaseous form, an extremely lethal toxic gas.

examples.text: Firefighters wore specialized breathing apparatus to protect themselves from fumes of hydrogen <w>cyanide</w>.
The accidental release of <w>cyanide</w> gas forced the evacuation of several nearby neighborhoods.

senses.sense_definition: Any chemical compound containing the monovalent group -CN or the cyanide anion.

examples.text: In organic chemistry, a <w>cyanide</w> is often referred to as a nitrile.
The laboratory analyzed the molecular structure to confirm the presence of a <w>cyanide</w> group.

senses.sense_definition: To treat or poison with cyanide, such as in metal extraction or extermination.

examples.text: The gold ore was finely crushed before the engineers <w>cyanided</w> the slurry to extract the metal.
Early twentieth-century farmers sometimes <w>cyanided</w> pest burrows to clear rodents from the fields.
